text:
Nina: Heads-up  vendor 'SeoulMetrics Co., Ltd.' invoiced Redwood, Inc. (US) and appended a note asking us to gross-up for a 7% Korean withholding tax. They DID charge 10% VAT on the invoice which seems odd for cross-border services. Any quick guidance? :thinking:

Juho: Quick flag  Korea VAT on international B2B services is usually 0% / outside scope if exported. If they charged 10% VAT and are now asking for a 7% gross-up that smells like confusion between VAT and withholding or a reseller/local nexus issue. Who is the invoiced Redwood entity?

Nina: Invoice PDF in Coupa shows payee Redwood, Inc. (US). Snippet: ```
Invoice#: 2026-09-03-SM
Supplier: SeoulMetrics Co., Ltd.
Biz reg: 110-88-77777
Amount: KRW 12,100,000 (approx USD 9,000)
VAT: KRW 1,100,000 (10%)
Vendor note: "Please gross-up 7% withholding tax so supplier receives net after Korean WHT."
Description: API analytics and insights (remote)
```

Maya: Do NOT pay gross-up until we verify. Two separate issues: (1) VAT charged on cross-border service to a US company looks wrong unless they have a Korean customer-facing supply; (2) Korean withholding (usually 3-22% depending on payment type) requires legal basis and often applies when Korean tax law treats the payment as Korean-source income. If Redwood, Inc. (US) is the payer, WHT might not apply.

TaxTeam: Confirming Maya. Ask vendor for: (A) explanation why they charged VAT (do they claim domestic supply?), (B) Korean tax authority notice or statement showing a 7% WHT applies to a payment from a US payer, (C) certificate of tax residency and any Korean WHT calculation, and (D) the contract clause if they assert a commercial gross-up. Also request a revised invoice clarifying VAT/tax treatment and the invoiced legal entity.

Juho: If they expect us to withhold on their behalf, they must provide remittance instructions and documentation for them to claim credit. If they instead want gross-up, they must show a contract clause requiring gross-up. Our policy: we don't gross-up unless contractually required or there's a clear statutory obligation.

Nina: I'll reply. Draft: "We cannot gross-up by default. Please provide the Korean tax/legal basis for the 7% withholding, a tax residency certificate, and reissue the invoice clarifying VAT and the invoiced entity. Payment will be held until validated." Good?

Maya: LGTM. Add: ask them to confirm the payment currency (we need KRW vs USD clarity) and whether they are asking us to increase the invoice by 7% or to have us withhold 7% on payment.

AP: I've placed invoice 2026-09-03-SM on HOLD in Coupa and flagged for tax docs.

invoice-bot: Payment status updated: HOLD set for invoice 2026-09-03-SM (SeoulMetrics Co., Ltd.) by AP  reason: awaiting vendor tax documentation and invoice clarification.

Nina: I'll send the note and CC Legal/Tax. Please tag here when vendor responds so we can route to TaxTeam quickly.

Juho: If vendor pushes back, Legal can review contract. But operationally we won't gross-up and won't accept VAT + gross-up without clear justification.

Maya: Also file note for records: if vendor provides a Korean tax notice showing WHT applies to payments from US companies, escalate for possible withholding obligations; otherwise decline gross-up and request corrected invoice (VAT reversed or 0% export, and no gross-up).

Nina: Thanks all 44d I'll paste their reply in this thread when it lands.
